pull.title: feat(driver): durable-outer-loop reference driver (lease/tick/budget/checkpoint)
pull.body:
## Summary
Gap3 from the session's post-merge maturity review: this library's own README describes the durable outer loop pattern in prose ("the host drives the loop") but never showed a concrete end-to-end example threading `scheduler`+`async`+`time` together. `kotoba-lang/kotoba-lang`'s `docs/lang/coverage.edn` tracks this explicitly under `:engineering-gaps/:async-runtime` ("gap is durable-outer-loop reference drivers threading async+time+scheduler, not a tokio").

New `kotoba.lang.scheduler.driver`:
- `lease` / `lease-valid?` -- a fencing token (`{:holder :epoch}`) and the "higher epoch wins" check, mirroring `kototama.fleet`'s own shared-store fencing model elsewhere in this org, kept storage-agnostic here (this library has no storage layer of its own)
- `checkpoint` -- `{:scheduler :budget :lease}`; documented honestly that `:budget`/`:lease` are plain EDN but `:scheduler` is not fully so (it carries the host-injected clock fn and each job's callback -- not a gap this driver invents, the same scope `kotoba.lang.scheduler` itself has)
- `run-tick!` -- one durable-outer-loop step: fires due jobs via `scheduler/tick`, spends the budget by the COUNT OF JOBS ACTUALLY FIRED (an idle tick with nothing due must not starve a waiting loop), stops firing once the budget is exhausted
- `exhausted?` / `drain-ready!` -- the host's own stop condition and ready-queue observation step

Same discipline every namespace in this stdlib already follows: pure data, pure transitions, no threads, no wall-clock, no I/O of its own.

## Test plan
- [x] `clojure -M:test` -- 16 tests, 39 assertions, 0 failures (10 pre-existing + 6 new)
- [x] `clojure -M:lint` -- 0 errors (11 pre-existing-style warnings, same "Redundant let"/"unused binding" style already present in `scheduler_test.cljc`, not introduced by this change)
